candidates.rationale: The useful behavior is alias-preserving reinterpretation of mutable storage, but core AtomicI8 has no public value view and current vstd cannot express the returned mutable reference's identity and writeback relation.

A useful contract must relate every returned atomic element to the same input storage and model later writeback. Current vstd exposes neither relation; preserving only the slice length would omit the method's essential semantics.
risks: slice aliasing and element identity are not modeled

candidates.rationale: A sound useful contract requires pointer validity, alignment, provenance, aliasing, lifetime, and atomic-access obligations plus an identity relation to the returned reference. This signature carries no vstd permission abstraction supporting those facts.

The useful facts are that the result contains the atomic's current value and that mutations write back into it. Without a public AtomicI8 value view, neither the initial value nor final writeback can be stated.
risks: mutable-reference writeback cannot be related to self

candidates.rationale: Current vstd cannot relate each returned integer to the corresponding hidden atomic value or express element-wise writeback. A length-only postcondition would not usefully specify the conversion.
risks: mutable slice writeback is not modeled

candidates.rationale: The result is the consumed atomic's hidden contained value. Core AtomicI8 has no public vstd view or permission in this signature with which to relate that value to self.
risks: no observable input value exists for a useful postcondition
